Audio: AAC HE-AACv2 stereo 44.1 kHz, continuous (no silence below -40 dB for 0.3 s or longer), mean -22.2 dB, peak -6.8 dB; the on-screen words follow a narration, so it is read as voice-over over a bed; not analysed for beats, third-party audio never reused. method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 (2 sheets, 6x2, both viewed); scene detect gt(scene,0.2) found one cut at 5.57 s only (the film is dark, so the other cuts score low); the other cuts were found by eye on dense sheets: fps=10 over 0-1.2 s (top 360 px crop, to read the word animation), 0.9-2.1 s, 2.6-3.8 s, 7.0-8.2 s, 8.8-10.0 s, and fps=5 over 9.6-11.9 s (6 dense sheets, all viewed). Spans accurate to about ±0.1 s. silencedetect + volumedetect on the audio. Colours read by eye, not sampled.

visual_language: A dark, cinematic finance-news short driven by a word-by-word caption. Medium: a mix of 3D renders (glass chart card, monitor, glossy spheres, abstract primitives on a reflective floor), a masked photo, pure type and a code-like line chart, all sitting in one navy-black world. Typography is the backbone: every word of the narration appears on screen in sync with the voice, one word at a time, as a two-line centred caption (line 1 regular, line 2 bold) in a neutral white grotesk sans with tight tracking, small (cap height about 2.5% of frame height), at the top of the frame, except one breath shot where the caption moves to the centre. Each word arrives with a 3D flip: it starts tilted away (about 60-80 degrees around the horizontal and vertical axes, grey and slightly above and right of its slot) and rotates flat into place while brightening to white in about 0.15-0.2 s (smooth ease-out); a new line starts by sliding in from the left, and the block re-centres as it grows. Rhythm: five shots in 11.9 s (about 2.4 s each), hard cuts on phrase boundaries, never on a beat; the caption carries across cuts and restarts with each new phrase. Moves are smooth: a long dolly-out (about 1 s), staggered rises (about 0.1 s apart), self-drawing lines, slow push-ins; accents are fast (light sweeps across glass, a cross flare at a peak). Palette: near-black to navy with a lighter blue-grey gradient from the upper left, one saturated electric blue as the only accent, white type and highlights, greyscale photos. Signature moments: the close-up that turns out to be a screen inside a wider world; the audience of glossy spheres rising; the pure-type question shot; the chart line that bursts out of the top of the frame with a flare.
look: Mostly real 3D (not flat) in a dark studio void. Materials: frosted glass cards with a bright blue emissive edge and a white grid printed on the glass; a dark monitor with a diagonal glass reflection streak; glossy deep-blue spheres with a bright rim highlight; matte to satin grey primitives with soft radial gradients; a saturated blue glass slab with a white specular sweep; a dark reflective floor with soft reflections. Light: one soft key from the upper left (visible light rays in the opening), blue rim and edge glows, soft contact shadows, glows and a cross-shaped lens flare as accents. Depth: moderate depth of field, back rows of spheres softer and darker; no heavy blur. Background: a soft diagonal gradient void (blue-grey upper left to near-black navy lower right), later a faint perspective grid plane. Photos are greyscale inside circular masks with thin ring lines.
code_translation: Not fully code-native (3D renders mixed with type and a chart). Per D55 the 3D parts are built as real 3D in code with three.js: glass cards and slabs as rounded boxes with MeshPhysicalMaterial (transmission, roughness for frost, clearcoat) plus an emissive blue edge and an animated specular sweep; glossy spheres with low roughness and a rim light; satin primitives with MeshStandardMaterial; a reflective floor (reflector or a mirrored plane with fade); one soft key from the upper left with god-ray sprites, a blue rim light and hemisphere fill; the screen-in-screen pull-back as a render-to-texture of the first scene mapped onto a screen mesh while the camera dollies out. The word-by-word caption is HTML/canvas type in the brand Persian font, whole words only and never split letters (rtl-grammar.md): each word flips in with a CSS 3D rotate (rotateX/rotateY about 70 degrees to 0, opacity and grey to white, about 0.18 s ease-out), words placed right to left, line 1 regular and line 2 bold; timing from audio.json word times. The circle photo is a CSS/canvas mask with SVG ring lines. The final chart is SVG or canvas on a perspective grid (CSS 3D or three.js plane) with a stroke-dashoffset draw, an additive cross-flare sprite and soft beam gradients; values and Persian digits per data-viz.md.
continuity: Caption as the spine: the narration appears word by word in the same place, size and two-weight style across every shot, so the film reads as one sentence even across hard cuts.
Word flip-in: each word rotates in from a 3D tilt and brightens into place, timed to the voice.
Screen inside a world: the opening close-up is revealed by a dolly-out to be a screen inside a larger scene.
Rising audience: simple glossy spheres rise from the bottom edge in staggered depth rows to mean 'people watching'.
Breath shot: one shot of pure type with the caption moved to the centre marks the turn or question in the story.
Cut through an empty frame: a hard cut lands on the bare background for a moment and the next subject pops in, so the dark world feels continuous.
Self-drawing line with a glowing tip: data appears as a line that draws itself, a light riding its head.
Peak bursts the frame: at the climax the line shoots out of the top edge with a cross flare and fanning light beams.
One accent colour: a single saturated blue carries every highlight (edges, spheres, glass, the line) against greyscale and navy.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy its finance-news story, English copy, figures (9.5%, two days, price chip), the press photo of a real official, the institutional seal, the monitor and audience scene or the abstract figure as designs, the 'APVULIA©' watermark, its audio, or its shot order one by one.

The caption is small (cap height about 2.5% of frame height) and the second line overlaps the first while it slides in: in our film the Persian caption must meet the minimum text size and hold times, never overlap, and sit inside the safe zone (safe-zones.md).
The word flip-in must use whole Persian words in a shaped font, placed right to left; joined letters are never split or rotated one by one (rtl-grammar.md).

The reference's palette is navy and electric blue: map it onto brand colour roles (dark neutral background, brand accent for every highlight), never its literal blue if the brand differs; colours were read by eye, not sampled.
Hard cuts land on dark frames and score low in scene detect: cut spans 3.65, 7.65 and 9.9 s were read by eye (±0.1 s); only 5.57 s was detected.
The masked-photo shot needs an image: use it only for an owner asset or an image the voice-over needs; never source photos of real people.
The film ends mid-sentence as a loop cut: our film needs its own ending (brand logo outro), not an abrupt stop.
Audio is third-party voice and bed; ignored, L2 and L6 build ours.
